name: Liebfrauenkirche Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Liebfrauenkirche on Kitzbühel's church hill features a massive bell tower, the famous six-ton Kaiser Bell, and an ornate baroque high altar.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Liebfrauenkirche in Kitzbühel rises picturesquely along the Lebenberg hill ridge at the northern edge of the historic town core. Together with the neighboring parish church of St. Andrew and the surrounding heritage cemetery, this gothic sanctuary forms the widely visible landmark crowning the rooftops of the town. Its imposing square fortification tower topped by a baroque onion dome bestows the church with an unmistakable silhouette. Designed as a two-story double church featuring a gothic lower church and an ornate baroque upper sanctuary, it is celebrated as one of the most remarkable sacred monuments in the Kitzbühel district. Due to its striking architecture and thunderous bronze bell, the sanctuary enjoys renown well beyond regional boundaries.

Route & Requirements

The sanctuary was first documented in 1373. Its defensive stone tower was erected in the mid-16th century, originally serving as a fortified civic refuge and belfry. Inside the belfry hangs the famed Kaiser Bell (Kaiserglocke, also known as the Frauenglocke), cast in 1845 by master founder Josef Georg Miller in Innsbruck. Weighing more than six metric tons, it is revered as one of the most melodious and deepest-toned historic bronze bells in Tyrol. The gothic lower church accommodates a historic ossuary (Karner) and a vaulted crypt featuring ribbed groin vaults. The contemplative sacred space delights through its balanced spatial harmony and sacred works by regional masters. The light-filled upper church was remodeled in the baroque style during the 18th century: luminous ceiling frescoes created by Simon Benedikt Faistenberger in 1739 depict the Assumption and Coronation of the Virgin Mary. The monumental high altar is graced with masterly carved figures and an early 16th-century late-Gothic Madonna and Child.

Visit & Arrival

The Liebfrauenkirche is open daily year-round from 08:00 to 18:00 free of charge. Traditional Marian devotions and festive liturgical services are held regularly. Arriving by rail: ÖBB trains to Kitzbühel or Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm, followed by a signposted ten-minute stroll through the old town up to the church hill. By car: via federal road B161, with parking at the Pfarrau central lot or the Hahnenkamm valley station.

Tips

The pathway up the hill involves stone steps and stepped inclines; rear road access to the cemetery gate is available for visitors with restricted mobility. Take time to explore the heritage cemetery adorned with forged iron funerary crosses. When the massive Kaiser Bell tolls on major feast days, its majestic resonance rings throughout the entire valley. Enjoy sweeping panoramic vistas across the Kitzbühel Alps from the viewing terrace above the churchyard.
